title: Home & everyday objects
goal: Name rooms and household objects, say where things are (in, on, under, next to…) and say what there is or isn't.
intro:
This unit takes you around a Nepali home. You'll learn the case ending **-मा** 'in/at/on' and the location words that combine with it — माथि 'on top', मुनि 'under', भित्र 'inside', छेउमा 'beside'.

You'll also put the verb **छ** to its most basic use: saying **there is / there are**. 'There is hot water in the room' is simply 'room-in hot water is': कोठामा तातो पानी छ.

vocab.note: घरमा 'at home'; घर जानु 'to go home'.
Also a rented room/flat: कोठा भाडामा लिनु 'to rent a room'. Bedroom = सुत्ने कोठा.
In traditional homes the kitchen is a pure space — ask before entering.
Formal/signs. In speech: ट्वाइलेट ṭwāileṭ or चर्पी charpi.
A flat roof terrace is कौसी kausi.
बत्ती गयो 'the power has gone'. बत्ती बाल्नु/निभाउनु 'turn the light on/off'.
Attached to the noun: घरमा, टेबलमा, काठमाडौंमा.
कोठाभित्र 'inside the room'; भित्र आउनुहोस् 'come in'.
X-को नजिक 'near X'; नजिकै 'very near, nearby'.
बीचमा 'in the middle'; X र Y-को बीचमा 'between X and Y'.

phrases.en: Please take your shoes off outside.
Is there hot water in the room?

phrases.note: पर्छ 'falls/lies' is used for locations of places.

grammar.title: Where things are: -मा and location words
grammar.body:
**-मा** means 'in', 'at' or 'on' and is attached to the end of the noun: कोठा**मा** 'in the room', टेबल**मा** 'on the table', काठमाडौं**मा** 'in Kathmandu'.

For more precise positions, Nepali uses location words placed **after** the noun (they're postpositions, not prepositions):

• Some attach directly: टेबल**माथि** 'on the table', खाट**मुनि** 'under the bed', घर**भित्र** 'inside the house', घर**बाहिर** 'outside the house'.
• Others take **-को** first and often **-मा** after: ढोकाको **छेउमा** 'beside the door', घरको **अगाडि** 'in front of the house', पसलको **पछाडि** 'behind the shop', स्कुलको **नजिक** 'near the school', दुई घरको **बीचमा** 'between two houses'.

With pronouns use the possessive: मेरो छेउमा 'next to me', तपाईंको अगाडि 'in front of you'.

examples.en: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the bed.
The bathroom is next to the stairs.
The shop is in front of the house.

grammar.title: 'There is / there are' with छ
grammar.body:
Nepali uses **छ** for existence. Put the place first, then the thing, then छ:

**[place]-मा [thing] छ।** — कोठामा खाट **छ** 'There is a bed in the room.'

For a plural subject use **छन्** (in casual speech छ is common for things). The negative is **छैन** 'there isn't' / **छैनन्** 'there aren't'. To ask, just raise the intonation: तातो पानी छ? 'Is there hot water?' The short answers are simply **छ** 'yes, there is' and **छैन** 'no, there isn't'.

**कोही** 'someone' and **केही** 'something' are handy here: कोही छ? 'Is anyone there?', केही छैन 'there's nothing'.

examples.en: There are two beds in the room.
There are no dishes in the kitchen.
Is there a shop near here?

dialogue.title: Renting a room
dialogue.setting: Sarah is looking at a flat to rent. The landlord (घरबेटी), an older man, shows her around.

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.native: आउनुहोस्, भित्र आउनुहोस्। यो बैठक हो।
lines.roman: āunuhos, bhitra āunuhos. yo baiṭhak ho.
lines.en: Come in, please. This is the living room.

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.en: The kitchen is behind the living room.

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.en: The bathroom is upstairs, next to the stairs.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Is there hot water in the bathroom?

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.en: Yes. There's a solar heater on the roof.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Is there a bed in the bedroom?

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.native: छ, एउटा दराज पनि छ। तर कुर्सी छैन।
lines.roman: chha, euṭā darāj pani chha. tara kursi chhaina.
lines.en: Yes, and there's a wardrobe too. But there's no chair.

culture: Always take your **shoes off** before entering a Nepali home, and certainly before entering the kitchen or the family shrine (पूजा कोठा). Many city houses are tall, narrow concrete buildings where the owner family (घरबेटी) lives on one floor and rents out rooms (कोठा) on others; the flat roof (**कौसी**) is used for drying clothes, sunbathing in winter and flying kites at Dashain. Power cuts (**बत्ती जाने**) were once scheduled daily as 'load-shedding' — the phrase बत्ती गयो! is still part of everyday life in many places.

tip.title: Being a guest
tip.body:
- The host says **भित्र आउनुहोस्** 'come in' and **बस्नुहोस्** 'please sit'. **-नुहोस्** is the polite 'please do'; with friends and children it's **आऊ**, **बस**.
- Shoes come off at the door: जुत्ता बाहिर खोल्नुहोस्.
- At the door, call out घरमा कोही हुनुहुन्छ? 'Anyone home?'

sentences.en: Please take your shoes off here.
Please sit in the living room.

tip.title: 'There is' = place-मा + thing + छ
tip.body:
- Say the place first, then the thing, then **छ**: कोठामा खाट **छ** 'there's a bed in the room'.
- More than one: **छन्**. None: **छैन** / **छैनन्**.
- To ask, just raise your voice: तातो पानी छ? The short answers are **छ** and **छैन**.

sentences.native: कोठामा एउटा खाट र एउटा दराज छ।
sentences.roman: koṭhāmā euṭā khāṭ ra euṭā darāj chha.
sentences.en: There's a bed and a cupboard in the room.
Is there hot water in the bathroom?
There's no pillow on the bed.
There are two pillows in the cupboard.
There's no water in the toilet.

tip.title: In, on, under: -मा, -माथि, -मुनि
tip.body:
- **-मा** 'in / at / on' sticks to the noun: टेबल**मा** 'on the table', कोठा**मा** 'in the room'.
- Location words come *after* the noun: टेबल**माथि** 'on top of the table', खाट**मुनि** 'under the bed'.
- Some take **-को** first: टेबल**को छेउमा** 'next to the table'. With people: **मेरो** छेउमा 'next to me'.
tip.pattern: thing + place-मा / place-माथि / place-को छेउमा + छ

sentences.en: The key is on the table.
My phone is under the chair.
Is the bag under the bed?
The chair is next to the table.
The key isn't in the cupboard.

tip.title: Front, back, between: -को + word
tip.body:
- **अगाडि** 'in front', **पछाडि** 'behind' and **बीचमा** 'between' take **-को** first: घर**को अगाडि**, भर्‍याङ**को पछाडि**.
- Between two things: X **र** Y**को बीचमा**.
- **माथि** 'upstairs', **तल** 'downstairs'; as adjectives **माथिल्लो** / **तल्लो** 'upper / lower'.

sentences.en: The kitchen is behind the stairs.
There's someone in front of the house.
The table is by the window.

sentences.native: बैठक र भान्साको बीचमा बाथरुम छ।
sentences.roman: baiṭhak ra bhānsāko bichmā bāthrum chha.
sentences.en: The bathroom is between the living room and the kitchen.
Brother's room is on the lower floor.
Mum is upstairs, on the roof.

tip.title: Where a place 'falls'
tip.body:
- For where a house or shop is, Nepali says it **पर्छ** 'falls': तपाईंको घर कहाँ **पर्छ**? 'Whereabouts is your house?'
- **नजिक** 'near', **नजिकै** 'right nearby', **टाढा** 'far'; from here = **यहाँबाट**.
- Load-shedding talk: बत्ती **गयो** 'the power's gone', बत्ती **आयो** 'it's back'.
tip.pattern: X + कहाँ पर्छ?  ·  यहाँबाट + नजिक / टाढा + छ

sentences.en: Our house is near the school.
How far is Thamel from here?
There's no light in the room.
The dishes are in the kitchen.
